title: Book Store API, part 1
idea: The Book Store API is the course's running project: a REST API for books. Part 1 builds the in-memory store, two `GET` routes and a validated `POST`.
points: Data lives in memory: a restart resets it, and chapter 5 adds a database.
Errors are JSON like `{ "error": "message" }`, sent with a matching status.
`POST` validates first, copies only the three named fields, and answers `201`.

hero.title: A POST request, start to finish

steps.caption: The client sends `POST /books` with a JSON body and a JSON `content-type` header.
`express.json()` reads the body and sets `req.body`, then passes the request on.
The route matches. The body has a title, author and year, so the check `isValid` passes.
The handler gives the book id 4 and pushes it onto `books`.
The handler replies `201` with the new book and a `Location` header holding its URL.
The client gets `201`. `books` now holds four books.
A second request has no `author`. It passes `express.json()` and reaches the route.
`isValid` is false, so the handler replies `400` at once. The store is never touched.
The client gets `400` and an `error` message. `books` is unchanged.

code.title: Read and create
code.caption: The Book Store so far, with a client that calls it. Press Run for the real output.

walk.text: The store: three starting books in an array, plus the next id to hand out.
`title` and `author` must be non-empty text; `year` a whole number.
`bookIndex` converts the URL id with `Number`. `fail` sends `{ error }` with a status.
Create the app and add `express.json()` so JSON bodies fill `req.body`.
`GET` routes: the list, and one book. A missing id gets 404 and a `return`.
`POST` validates, copies only the three fields, and answers 201 with a `Location` URL.
A client calls the API, prints each status and body, then closes the server.

pitfalls: `req.params.id` is a string: convert it with `Number()` before comparing ids.
Always `return` after an error reply, or the handler keeps running and may still change data.
Send `content-type: application/json` from clients; otherwise `req.body` stays `undefined`.

quiz.why: `'2' === 2` is false, so the first lookup finds nothing. `Number('2')` is 2, which matches the second book.

takeaway: A handler checks its input, changes data, and answers exactly once.

starters: Why return 201 instead of 200 when a book is created?
What is the difference between `req.params` and `req.query`?
Why keep books in an array instead of a file or database?
